reviews.text: Bad karma for not playing…. I installed Fretello because I needed a simple guitar tuner app, and previous apps had become bloated, pricey and unusable. Fretello had turned into another bloated, pricey mess. Also unusable, because I couldn't even make it past the first screen without paying a pricey subscription. Great idea, some issues though.. So, this was a genius idea. Free guitar lessons, test songs and warm ups, a digital guitar tuner, etc. This app really thought of it all. However, with all of these great features, I was so disappointed that this just wasn’t the app for learning guitar! If you already know how to play the guitar, you know how to tune and all of the parts on a guitar, and you’re just trying to practice extra, you’ve found the right place. But for beginners, this was so not easy! I had to keep googling terms and parts, it was like the people in the video were speaking a different language! The guitar tuner was completely unusable and no matter how hard I tried, something always was off. And, guys, this isn’t my first music lesson! I take piano lessons (which I’ve been playing since I was seven) and practice voice. I know notes and I understand the music symbols and timings. I was so excited that I had this untouched guitar sitting in my closet and that I’d finally learn it, and was so disappointed to find that this app really was far too good sounding to really be true. Just a few suggestions: 
1: For VERY VERY new musicians, you should give them basic lessons on notes and symbols.
2: You should definitely make a better guitar tuner that’s more accurate. 
3: You should have an in depth video explaining all of the parts of a guitar. 

That’s all! I hope this was helpful to anyone considering downloading this! I also hope you put my suggestions into action, Fretello Music!

Great learning tool. I started using Fretello a few months ago. 
Pros- I really like that it allows you to customize your lessons based on the style of music you are interested in mastering. I also really like that it uses standard tab for the lessons (unlike some other apps I’ve tried that rely on gimmicky interfaces). I think the repetition in the lessons is also very helpful in building muscle memory and I can notice improvements in my playing each session.
Cons- My only real complaint is that it doesn’t provide any feedback on how well you are hitting notes and keeping time. It would be awesome if this was added and you received some sort of grade after each lesson. Then you could see which lessons you didn’t do well on and could repeat if you wanted to improve.

I'd like to say that guitar playing, like any other artistic skill, is a result of the effort and passion that you put into learning it. I've read some of the negative reviews and comments and I'm certain that a majority of the people who have left them are looking for miracle app that will magically allow them to suddenly be able to play the latest boy band hit or Taylor Swift song and this app isn't going to do that for it's users. That being said, I've been wanting to find an app to help me structure my valuable practice time to help me carry my guitar playing skills to the next level and I believe I have found it in this app. To the developers: Thanks again and ignore all of the haters/posers!!

Awkward and Unclear. Fretello seems like a really good attempt at a guitar learning app. However the execution is severely lacking. For example, it begins by asking you to determine your skill level, I told the app that I could play complex melodies and rhythms (so not a beginner). It then began me on an A minor Pentatonic scale, warming up with two strings at a time for 5 minutes while it counted down on a timer. Needless to say, that got stale very quickly. 

Next came a tempo detector. The app listens to you play and inaccurately assigns you a tempo to play the exercises with. For example, it asked me to play the A minor Pentatonic scale as quickly and cleanly as I could. Upon doing so, I was assigned the tempo of 20bpm. 

I attempted the third exercise and that's when I had enough. I was unable to change the tempo I was assigned or even go back to let it detect another tempo. The metronome counted me in (again, at 20bpm) and the metronome wasn't even accurate! The measure was in 3/4 time and contained only eighth notes. The metronome seemed to be clicking twice per eighth note (again, at 20bpm). At that point, I had enough. 

Again, this app seems like a great attempt but the material presented and the interface only serve to frustrate. Until an update or better version of this app comes out, it would be infinitely more beneficial to learn what the cycle of 4ths is and practice your scales and chords around that. Then, begin transcribing and learning songs you like to learn how to play through osmosis. Apps and technology are great, but all the answers you need are on the records you own (or in your iTunes, I suppose) and in the songs you love.

Good try Fretello, I look forward to trying this app again once it has been reworked.

It’s the right idea. I have been looking for a guitar app that can teach me more about the theory of music and help me to understand and read music faster. At the same time, I am an at home guitar player and just want to be able to play my favourite songs and show off when friends and family come around.

No that being said, I do practice daily, but I find that there isn’t enough guidance on the app or a step by step guide you can follow. 

It would be great if they could compile the lessons in order of importance, like a follow along lesson plan, and while you work through and master the lessons, you get ratings that help you see where you need to put in a little more practice.

I find that the lessons are a little all over the place. And then the song selection is very limited. Some other guitar apps have a much larger selection, but lack in the theory side. So if they could increase the song selection, add backing tracks to it that you can slow down and have real time feedback where the app can show you where or how you have gone wrong, it will feel more personal, like you have a real guitar teacher there with you.

All in all, I think the developers are going in the right direction, but there is still a lot more that could be added to the app to make it more interactive, more fun, and easier to follow along a progressive line of improving skills and song repertoire.
